pairs.subject: companion-runtime
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/athena/[id]/message/route.ts:75 The SSE adapter starts a turn for any POST on a thread without any per-conversation claim, and the turn's event union ends only in settled or error, so two messages sent to one thread at once run two model streams into one transcript, and a stopped turn has no interrupted verdict.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/athena/[id]/message/route.ts:75 The adapter itself is clean: it only renames events and the turn is a function returning typed events. But there is no lock keyed on thread identity and no declared reject/queue/supersede policy (grep for lock/concurrent/in-flight in the route, turn.ts and athena-threads.ts found nothing). AthenaEvent (turn.ts:41) has no interrupted verdict, and the adapter sends done {ok:true} on every path (route.ts:96).

src/app/api/athena/gate.ts:238 Every Athena leg goes through runToolLoop, where legKind is a required field (src/lib/llm/tool-loop.ts:81 `legKind: LlmLegKind;`). The cycle states "athena_cycle" at deps.ts:156. Unknown usage is carried as null, never 0 (turn.ts AthenaPersistInput). The leg names refer to the feature rather than the situation, which is a minor gap against the naming advice.

src/app/api/athena/proposals/[id]/resolve/route.ts:143 At acceptance the same validator, built from the one ATHENA_ACTIONS table, is run again. A dropped kind is retired with a stated reason (line 147), and the required role is read from the spec rather than a second list (line 172). Executors are bound by Record<AthenaActionId, ...> in actions-execute.ts, so a missing executor fails to compile.

src/app/api/cron/athena/route.ts:118 An atomic once-per-period claim is taken before any spend and released on skip or throw. Orgs with a live turn are skipped and counted (cycle.ts isLiveTurn). The ceiling is declared (maxLegs: 1 and budgetMs at deps.ts:159). There is no identity writer in the cycle deps, the proposal queue has a reaper (sweepOrgProposals), and degraded runs return 207. Caveat: the claim is a durable row, so a process killed mid-run suppresses that org for the rest of the day's period (bounded, not forever).

src/app/api/cron/athena/route.ts:143 Report-or-absorb is decided inside runOrgCycle before anything is landed (the thread is minted only on land, deps.ts). Absorbed runs and outcomes are counted separately from briefed ones (route.ts:136), and every skip reason is a named, counted value, so a quiet run can be told apart from one that never ran.

src/app/api/athena/gate.ts:204 The host wires store, model leg and grounding into AthenaTurnDeps and passes them in at call time. turn.ts imports only types and sibling athena modules, and runs against fakes in turn.test.ts. Caveats: the runtime is a module inside the host package (cycle.ts reaches @/lib/db/athena-threads for deriveThreadTitle), and there is no second turn channel yet to prove the seam.

pairs.registryProposal: autonomous-cycle-hosting says to keep the single-flight claim in process memory so a dead process releases it. On serverless cron with overlapping invocations no process memory is shared, so a durable compare-and-set claim scoped to a period is the only workable guard. The technique could name a period-scoped durable claim, released on every non-crash exit, as the accepted form for serverless hosts.
